verdict_reason: Only one open question was both load-bearing and answerable on this host: migrating ${ARGN} to PARSE_ARGV (language OQ 2). It affects MUST CMK-LANG-04 and the cmake-modernize rewrite step, and it was measured in this phase on 3.31.12, 4.3.4 and 4.4.2; scratch is in /home/mherwig/.cache/cmake-measure-scratch/parse-argv-migration/. PARSE_ARGV keeps a quoted list as one element with an escaped ';'. An unquoted forward then passes it as one argument. `set(p_KW ${p_KW})` right after the parse restores the legacy splitting. The answer is pinned as a LANG-04 migration clause in the Authoring notes, and no new ID is minted. Every other open item is classified as residue with no MUST impact (R1-R10), host-cannot-measure (Windows, hosted runner, Bazel, g++, 4.0-4.2), a dated re-check (D1-D8) or an owner default.

LANG-04 migration clause (measured this phase). Migrating ${ARGN} to PARSE_ARGV changes callers: a quoted list to a multi-value keyword arrives as one escaped element and forwards as one argument; a quoted list to a one-value keyword arrives whole. For list-valued multi-value keywords, add set(<prefix>_<KW> ${<prefix>_<KW>}) right after the parse. Severity: MUST for new public commands; for migrating existing ones, MUST with the flatten line or a changelog entry; SHOULD for private helpers. cmake-modernize never rewrites a public parse without the flatten line.

Rules to DROP: (1) consumable-library's TGT-01..09 copy. (2) Reserved CONAN-19, VCPKG-19/20 and PKG-05..07 are never emitted or reused.
